answers.studentAnswerText: Hydroxide ion attacks carbon from the side opposite to chlorine. A transition state forms where both OH and Cl are partially bonded. Cl- leaves, causing complete inversion of configuration (Walden inversion).
answers.diagramDescription: Chemical structure drawing of CH3Cl with curved arrow from :OH- to central carbon; bracketed transition state with partial bonds dashed to HO and Cl and negative charge; final product with inverted tetrahedral geometry.
